summary: Anthropic S1 will be the most important demand signal for the entire AI infrastructure food chain
summary_extended: Baker argues that Anthropic's post-IPO quarterly earnings will serve as the single most important demand signal for the entire AI infrastructure supply chain, functioning as a 'pace car' that sets the pace for the whole industry. His reasoning is that Anthropic is currently the leading pure-play frontier AI model company, and its revenue trajectory directly determines compute demand, which cascades downstream through the entire capex chain: if Anthropic's growth slows, it sequentially pressures GPU demand (Nvidia), advanced packaging and leading-edge logic (TSMC), and high-bandwidth memory (Micron, SK Hynix). Baker explicitly maps out this dependency chain, calling the Anthropic S1 and subsequent earnings 'the most important signal the entire industry has' for validating or invalidating the AI capex supercycle thesis. The investment implication is that investors in AI infrastructure names — particularly semiconductor and datacenter suppliers — should treat Anthropic's IPO disclosures and quarterly results as the primary leading indicator for position sizing across the entire AI infrastructure trade.
detail: Baker argues Anthropic's quarterly earnings post-IPO will be the 'pace car' for the entire industry. If Anthropic slows, it cascades: SpaceX AI → Nvidia → TSMC → Micron → SK Hynix. The S1 will validate or invalidate the AI capex supercycle thesis.

ticker_audit.reasoning: Anthropic is the explicit subject of the thesis — Baker's entire argument centers on its IPO and post-IPO earnings as the pace car for the industry.
Baker explicitly names Nvidia as a direct downstream beneficiary/victim of Anthropic's demand trajectory — if Anthropic slows, Nvidia GPU demand slows with it.
Baker explicitly includes TSMC in the cascade chain as the leading-edge logic and advanced packaging supplier that depends on Anthropic-driven compute demand.
Baker explicitly names Micron as part of the HBM/memory supply chain that is downstream of Anthropic's compute demand — a direct beneficiary or victim of the pace car dynamic.

SK Hynix is not US-listed and therefore should be excluded per audit rules; it is a Korean-listed equity. While Baker may have implied HBM producers broadly, only US-listed equities qualify, and MU already captures the US-listed HBM angle.
